scope: Proposition 3.1 (The half-cylinder inverse pairing) of the manuscript “Disk transfer representations and confined bridge mass” (preprints/Disk-transfer-representations-and-confined-bridge-mass-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d64dc634fe49d994), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For N ≥ 3 and generic distinct rapidities sufficiently near zero, define Cij = 1 xi + qxj (1 ≤ i, j ≤ N). Then ∑ i xi − c ∑ i̸=j ei(ηi+ηj) Hij(η) = 1T (CT + qC)−1 1. (3.1) The scalar pairing on the right has a removable continuation to a neighborhood of homogeneous rapidities. This does not assert that the matrix inverse itself extends to coincident rapidities.
